verdicts.tldr: the snapshot's landing page tells the reviewer outbound links are dead, and they silently open master's render on gno.land
verdicts.details: Index writes 'transactions, search and links outside the preview do not work' (comment.go:191-192), while mapURL returns c.Live + target for every in-site path the crawl did not capture (crawl.go:405) and Live defaults to https://gno.land (main.go:28, wired at main.go:70 and 127). The same file's footer says the opposite one screen away: 'links out of the preview go to the live site' (comment.go:88). A reviewer who follows such a link, on a realm the cap dropped for instance, is looking at master's render of a realm this pull request may have changed, having been told the link could not work. Fix: make the index sentence match the footer, naming the live origin and saying the page it reaches is master's, not this branch's.
verdicts.evidence: crawl.go:405 `return c.Live + target + frag`; main.go:28 `defaultLive = "https://gno.land"`, main.go:70 `fs.StringVar(&cfg.live, "live", defaultLive, "origin used for links the snapshot does not contain")`, main.go:127 `Live: strings.TrimSuffix(cfg.live, "/")`; comment.go:191-192 against comment.go:88.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -n 'return c.Live + target' misc/gnopreview/crawl.go and grep -n 'defaultLive|Live:' misc/gnopreview/main.go: the uncaptured-link fallback is the live origin, default https://gno.land, so the index page's sentence is false

verdicts.tldr: a realm pulled in by a changed realm is filed under 'affected through a changed package', and no package is named
verdicts.details: BuildPlan puts every changed package into changedPkgs, realms included (plan.go:220-221), and dependents() seeds from changedPkgs (plan.go:240), so a realm that imports a changed realm lands in p.Realms. examples/gno.land/r/gnops/valopers/proposal/proposal.gno:7 imports gno.land/r/gnops/valopers, so a pull request touching valopers alone prints proposal under '**Realms affected through a changed package (1)**' (comment.go:75). p.ChangedPkgs is empty in that case, so the `_changed:` line that would name the culprit is skipped (comment.go:76-78) and the reader is told a package changed when none did. Fix: label the section from what seeded it, or say 'through a changed realm' when ChangedPkgs is empty.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn 'gno.land/r/gnops/valopers"' examples/gno.land/r/gnops/valopers/proposal/*.gno -> proposal.gno:7 `valopers "gno.land/r/gnops/valopers"`; plan.go:220-221 enters every changed package, realm or not, into changedPkgs; plan.go:240 `for _, p := range dependents(pkgs, changedPkgs)`; comment.go:76 `if len(p.ChangedPkgs) > 0`.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -n 'gno.land/r/gnops/valopers"' examples/gno.land/r/gnops/valopers/proposal/proposal.gno for the realm-to-realm import, then plan.go:216 (realms enter changedPkgs) and plan.go:295 (dependents seeds from changedPkgs)

verdicts.tldr: a push the paths filter misses leaves a stale snapshot under a comment claiming it is rebuilt on every push
verdicts.details: The footer sentence is emitted whenever pr != "" (comment.go:89-91), and no rendered commit appears anywhere in the body. pr-preview.yml triggers only on pushes touching examples/gno.land/**, gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/**, gno.land/cmd/gnoweb/**, contribs/gnodev/**, misc/gnopreview/** or the workflow file (lines 17-26), so a later commit under gnovm/ or gno.land/pkg/sdk/ renders nothing and updates nothing. A gnovm change is exactly the kind that changes what a realm renders, and the reviewer has no way to tell the snapshot is of an older head. Fix: put the rendered head SHA in the footer so the claim is checkable.
verdicts.evidence: pr-preview.yml:17-26 paths filter, no gnovm/ or gno.land/pkg/sdk/ entry; comment.go:89-91 `if pr != "" { ... "Rebuilt on every push to this PR; removed when PR #%s closes." }`; no SHA anywhere in comment.go.
verdicts.verify_by: sed -n '14,27p' .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml for the paths filter, and grep -n 'Rebuilt on every push' misc/gnopreview/comment.go

verdicts.tldr: with no base URL the comment still lists every rendered realm, which is what the godoc promises
verdicts.details: pairGrid (comment.go:99-102) and shotGrid (comment.go:130-133) do return "" on an empty base, but the listing does not: gnoweb mode prints each of p.Realms through link(), which degrades to a plain backticked path when base is empty (comment.go:29-34, 43-45), and the default mode prints '**Changed realms (n)**' with the same fallback (comment.go:60-66). So the comment lists what was rendered, without links, exactly as the godoc says; only the images are absent, and an image cannot be referenced at all without a base URL. The workflow never takes this path either: the render job is gated on vars.GNOWEB_PREVIEW_BASE_URL != '' and always passes -base-url (pr-preview.yml:43, 101). Fix: none needed.
verdicts.evidence: comment.go:30-32 `if base == "" { return "`" + label + "`" }`; comment.go:44 `b.WriteString("- " + link(urlOf(r), r) + "\n")` in gnoweb mode and comment.go:63 in the default mode; pr-preview.yml:43 `if: vars.GNOWEB_PREVIEW_BASE_URL != ''`, line 101 `-base-url "$BASE_URL"`.
verdicts.refuted_by: comment.go:31 `return "`" + label + "`"` — link() degrades to the bare realm name, so comment.go:44 and comment.go:63 still emit one line per rendered realm with base empty.
verdicts.verify_by: go run ./misc/gnopreview render -changed <a gnoweb file list> -out /tmp/p with no -base-url, then grep -c '<img' /tmp/p/comment.md against jq '.shots|length' /tmp/p/preview.json

verdicts.tldr: the preview homepage offers source and help links the crawl may never have captured, so the row 404s
verdicts.details: Index skips a realm whose render page is missing (comment.go:170 `if _, ok := c.pages[u]; !ok { continue }`) and then writes the source and help links on the same row unconditionally (comment.go:173-176). Those two are separate seeds (crawl.go:91-92 `add(u + "$source")`, `add(u + "$help")`), and Run logs and continues on a fetch error, on a non-200 and on a spent per-file budget (crawl.go:130-140), so either can be missing from c.pages while the render page is present. Only captured pages are written, so the reviewer clicks 'source' on the landing page and gets the static host's 404; no test exercises Index at all, the package has none. Fix: guard each tab link on c.pages the way the row itself is guarded, and omit the link when the page was not captured.
verdicts.evidence: comment.go:170 guards on the render page alone; comment.go:173-176 emits `source help` with no lookup. crawl.go:131-136 `fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, " ! %s: %v\n", u, err)` / `" ! %s: HTTP %d\n"` then continue. grep -rn 'Index(' misc/gnopreview: one call site (main.go:141), zero tests. The finder's fixture fails at this head: 'index links _t/source/ for a realm whose page was never captured'.
verdicts.verify_by: Index(&Plan{Realms:["gno.land/r/x/leaf"]}, crawler holding only "/r/x/leaf") and grep the output for _t/source/

verdicts.tldr: a pull request that only changes the preview tool renders no preview, so the crawler's own change is never exercised
verdicts.details: pr-preview.yml triggers on misc/gnopreview/** and on the workflow file itself (lines 24-26), while gnowebPaths carries only gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/, gno.land/cmd/gnoweb/ and contribs/gnodev/ (plan.go:28-32). A change to the crawler, the slugger or the comment writer therefore sets Gnoweb false with no changed realm, and the job stops at the skip gate (pr-preview.yml:79-82). It is not a wasted run — the step still builds the binary and runs plan (line 77), so the tool is compile-checked — but no crawl, no snapshot and no comment ever runs against the changed tool. Fix: add "misc/gnopreview/" to gnowebPaths so a change to the tool renders the seed sample.
verdicts.evidence: pr-preview.yml:24-26 `- misc/gnopreview/**`, `- .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml`; plan.go:28-32 gnowebPaths lists three trees, neither of those among them; plan.go:212-215 sets Gnoweb only on a gnowebPaths prefix; pr-preview.yml:79-82 sets skip=true when gnoweb is false and realms is empty.
verdicts.verify_by: read .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml paths against gnowebPaths, then run gnopreview plan with changed=misc/gnopreview/crawl.go and read the emitted JSON: gnoweb false, realms empty

verdicts.tldr: a failing plan step stays green and the job dies minutes later in render, pointing the reader at the wrong step
verdicts.details: GitHub runs a run: block as bash -e {0}, and pr-preview.yml sets no shell:, no defaults: and no pipefail. In `"$RUNNER_TEMP/gnopreview" plan -changed changed.txt | tee plan.json` (line 78) the pipeline's status is tee's, so any failure of the just-built binary leaves plan.json empty and the step green. jq then reads that empty file, prints nothing and exits 0, so the comparison against "no" fails, skip stays unset, and the job goes on to build gnodev and render before hitting the same error. Fix: add `set -o pipefail` to the step, or a defaults.run.shell: bash block, so the plan failure is the red step.
verdicts.evidence: grep -n 'shell:|defaults:|pipefail|set -e' .github/workflows/pr-preview*.yml: no matches. My run: `bash -e -c 'false | tee plan.json; echo rc after pipe=$?; echo reached-next-step'` printed `rc after pipe=0` then `reached-next-step`; the same command under `bash -eo pipefail` exited 1 without printing. jq -r 'if .gnoweb or (.realms | length > 0) then "yes" else "no" end' on the empty plan.json: rc=0, output empty, so the gate prints 'GATE: skip NOT set -> job continues'.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -n 'shell:|defaults:|pipefail|set -e' .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml returns nothing; then bash -e -c 'false | tee x; echo rc=$?' prints rc=0 and continues, and jq -r 'if .gnoweb or (.realms | length > 0) then "yes" else "no" end' on an empty file prints nothing with rc=0

verdicts.tldr: the help link can vanish from every preview comment with no test noticing
verdicts.details: tabs() emits both ` · [source](…/_t/source/)` and ` · [help](…/_t/help/)` for every changed and indirectly affected realm (comment.go:154), and TestCommentRealms asserts only the source URL (plan_test.go:199). The string `_t/help` occurs nowhere in any test file of the package: its only two occurrences in the tree are comment.go:154 and comment.go:174, so deleting the help half of the format string and its two arguments keeps the suite green. The help page is what shows a realm's exported functions, the stated reason boards2 is in the seed sample (plan.go:40). Fix: add "https://example.test/pr-7/r/x/leaf/_t/help/" to the want list in TestCommentRealms.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn '_t/help' misc/gnopreview/ -> comment.go:154 and comment.go:174 only, no test file; plan_test.go:195-204 want list carries "https://example.test/pr-7/r/x/leaf/_t/source/" and no help URL. The finder's mutation run records M6 tabs() help link: GREEN (mutation survives).
verdicts.verify_by: sed -i 's| . \[help\](%s%s/_t/help/)||; s|, base, u, base, u)|, base, u)|' comment.go && go test ./... ; expect a failure, observe ok

verdicts.tldr: a package under a dot-directory would be loaded and previewed, despite the guard that reads as excluding one
verdicts.details: filepath.WalkDir prunes a directory only on an fs.SkipDir return; the guard at plan.go:114 returns nil, which drops the dotted directory entry itself and still descends into everything under it. A package at examples/gno.land/r/.staging/foo, a gnomod.toml plus one .gno file, would therefore be registered in pkgs, enter the dependents graph and be rendered. Nothing under examples/gno.land is dot-prefixed today, so the guard protects nothing and misstates what it does; it is a latent risk, not a live defect. Fix: return fs.SkipDir for a dot-prefixed directory, keeping return nil for the non-directory case.
verdicts.evidence: plan.go:114-116 `if !d.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(d.Name(), ".") { return nil }`; find <head>/examples/gno.land -type d -name '.*' | wc -l -> 0.
verdicts.verify_by: read filepath.WalkDir's contract for a nil return on a directory entry, then `find examples/gno.land -type d -name '.*'`

verdicts.tldr: a realm the pull request deletes leaves no trace in the plan or in the comment
verdicts.details: LoadPkgs walks the head tree (plan.go:107-110), so a realm the branch removed has no entry in byDir. BuildPlan's only branch for a changed path is `if p := byDir[path.Dir(f)]; p != nil && !p.Ignore` (plan.go:220), and the nil lookup falls through recording nothing. The realm is then absent from ChangedRealms, from Realms and from Dropped, which counts cap losses alone (plan.go:256-258), so a pull request whose whole effect is that a realm stopped existing produces no comment at all, or one that never mentions it. Fix: record a changed path whose package is missing at head and name it in the comment as removed.
verdicts.evidence: plan.go:109 `base := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(pkgRoot))` with root the head checkout; plan.go:220 is the only branch consuming a changed path, and it has no else; plan.go:257 `plan.Dropped = len(realms) - maxRealms` is the cap alone.
verdicts.verify_by: read the byDir lookup against LoadPkgs' root: pkgs is built from the head tree alone, and no branch records a changed path whose package is missing

verdicts.tldr: the fixture's realm order pins nothing: every assertion in that test is a substring check
verdicts.details: ChangedRealms is indeed always sorted in production, BuildPlan filling it from sortedKeys(changedPkgs) (plan.go:229-234), and the fixture at plan_test.go:237 does pass [leaf, fresh]. But TestCommentBeforeAfter asserts only through strings.Contains over a want list (plan_test.go:245-255), so no bullet ordering is pinned and adding a sort inside Comment would leave the test green. The unrealistic fixture misleads no future change and costs the reader nothing. Fix: none needed.
verdicts.evidence: plan_test.go:252 `if !strings.Contains(got, want)`, the only assertion over the comment body; the want list at 245-251 carries image URLs and two captions, no realm ordering.
verdicts.refuted_by: plan_test.go:252 `if !strings.Contains(got, want) {` — containment only, so the order of ChangedRealms is never compared.

verdicts.tldr: the dependents-side ignore guard is pinned by a test, and both guards are forward-looking rather than dead
verdicts.details: The test tree writes examples/gno.land/r/x/ignored with `ignore = true`, importing p/x/base/v0 (plan_test.go:44-47), and the case 'transitive dependency pulls both dependents' changes p/x/base/v0 and asserts Realms is exactly [gno.land/r/x/leaf, gno.land/r/x/other] (plan_test.go:77-82, compared with reflect.DeepEqual at line 143), which fails the moment `pkgs[p].Ignore` at plan.go:241 is removed. The claim that nothing pins either guard is therefore wrong. The live tree does carry no ignore = true under examples/gno.land, both files sitting in examples/quarantined/ outside pkgRoot, but ignore is a supported gnomod.toml flag and the guards are defensive, not unreachable code. Fix: none needed; the one gap worth closing is a case changing a file inside r/x/ignored, which would pin plan.go:220.
verdicts.evidence: plan_test.go:45-47 writes gnomod.toml with `ignore = true` plus a lib.gno importing gno.land/p/x/base/v0; plan_test.go:78-82 changes examples/gno.land/p/x/base/v0/lib.gno with wantRealms [leaf, other]; plan_test.go:143 `if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Realms, tc.wantRealms)`. grep -rl 'ignore *= *true' --include=gnomod.toml examples -> examples/quarantined/gno.land/r/moul/outfmt/gnomod.toml, examples/quarantined/gno.land/r/jaekwon/dao/gnomod.toml.
verdicts.refuted_by: plan_test.go:46 `"module = \"gno.land/r/x/ignored\"\nignore = true\n"` with plan_test.go:80 `wantRealms: []string{"gno.land/r/x/leaf", "gno.land/r/x/other"}` — the ignored realm is a dependent of the changed package and is asserted absent.
verdicts.verify_by: grep -rl ignore --include=gnomod.toml examples | grep -v '^examples/quarantined/' returns nothing
